key_insight: Choosing the right quantum-trajectory unraveling can significantly lower the average magic in noisy random circuits, but it does not eliminate rare high-magic trajectories that still dominate classical simulation cost.
engineering_relevance: For stabilizer-based quantum simulators, unraveling design can reduce typical resource requirements under local dephasing, yet worst-case trajectories remain a key bottleneck for scalable simulation.
method: Studied Haar-random and T-doped random Clifford brickwork circuits with local dephasing noise of strength p.
Compared the canonical Pauli-jump unraveling with the full two-parameter family of minimal unravelings.
Optimized the unraveling to minimize trajectory-averaged stabilizer Rényi entropy (magic).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the optimal unraveling lowers the extensive magic density by a p-dependent factor while preserving linear scaling with system size, and produces a broad trajectory-to-trajectory distribution with many high-magic outliers.
watch_item: An unraveling that minimizes average magic may still leave enough rare high-magic trajectories to control simulation cost, so average-case gains may overstate practical speedups.
paper_title: Magic in quantum trajectory unravelings of noisy random quantum circuits
